newsitem.title: USA: U.S. refiners eye North Sea, Latam crudes. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. refiners eye North Sea, Latam crudes. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]

text.p: U.S. refiners eyed a range of North Sea and Latin American crudes on Monday, although actual transactions were limited, traders said.
In one significant deal, Argentine YPF placed 950,000 barrels of Canadon Seco crude oil at $3.90 to $4.00 (corrects price) under October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing on an fob basis.
The cargo, which loads August 24-25, was sold to a major U.S. refiner.
Elsewhere in the region, U.s. refiners are looking for alternatives to Colombian Cano Limon after more rebel attacks on the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline.

Amoco and Exxon have been probing the market for prompt deliveries of similar grades since last week, when Colombian state oil company Ecopetrol declared force majeur on liftings. Force majeur has been in place since the morning of July 6.
Amoco bought two 500,000 barrel cargoes of Cano Limon last month from Elf Aquitaine and Coastal. The cargoes are due to co-load at Covenas on an LR2 tanker dubbed "Alta" on July 22-26.
As a result of the shutdown, the vessel is not expected to load until sometime after July 28, traders said.
Cano Limon is currently priced around $2.30 a barrel under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for August loading.
Colombian Vasconia crude, which is not affected by the unrest, was assessed around $3.00 under WTI fob.
From the North Sea, a U.S. company has one remaining Brent cargo for August 25-30 delivery, asking around WTI minus 30 cents a barrel.
A Norwegian company, meanwhile, is offering 500,000 barrels of Heidrun for mid-August delivery, asking about $1.00 a barrel under WTI.
